newsitem.title: POLAND: Zasada to up Star stake to 66 percent.
newsitem.headline: Zasada to up Star stake to 66 percent.

text.p: Polish automotive group Sobieslaw Zasada Centrum SA will increase its stake in truck maker Star SA to 66 percent from the current 28 percent, officials of the two companies said on Monday.
Zasada's president Wincenty Zeszuta said his company would buy a 30-million-zloty new share issue approved by a general shareholders' meeting of Star on Monday.
"Today, the general shareholders' meeting decided to increase Star's share capital by 30.5 million zlotys, which will be bought by Sobieslaw Zasada Centrum," Zeszuta told reporters.
The decision buried hopes of a consortium led by Polski Bank Rozwoju SA (PBR) to increase its stake in Star.
Zeszuta said that after the acquisition Star would begin a cooperation with Daimler-Benz AG's subsidiary, Mercedes-Benz, which is a partner of Zasada.
Under the cooperation, Star will start manufacturing trucks with Mercedes engines next year, Zeszuta said.
Star president Roman Musial said his company wanted to invest 84 million zlotys, including 30.5 million from Zasada, in modernisation until the year 2001.
Musial said Zasada would pay in instalments for the Star stake. It would pay 7.6 million zlotys by July 10 and the next instalment would be contributed by June 30, 1998, he said without elaborating.
